sources.title: Hello GPT-4o
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026. May 13, 2024 launch makes GPT-4o available through the API for text and image input and text output. It describes one end-to-end multimodal network but publishes no nominal total or active parameter count. Broader audio/video demonstrations and later access are not substituted for this dated API snapshot; the Transformers topic tag is not a technical architecture disclosure.

sources.title: GPT-4o model documentation
sources.evidence: Fresh complete Markdown fetched October 27 identifies gpt-4o-2024-05-13 under GPT-4o and marks it shut down, but publishes neither total nor active parameter counts. The page defaults to August 6, 2024; its 16,384 output limit and later-default features are not transferred to May. The official documentation retrieval was also reopened; the earlier dedicated May-snapshot Markdown attempt returned 404.

sources.title: Foundry Models sold by Azure: GPT-4o capabilities
sources.evidence: The exact GPT-4o 2024-05-13 row documents 128,000 input tokens, a separate 4,096 output limit, text/image processing and parallel function calling. Used as first-party provider corroboration for this precise model version, not for OpenAI service retirement or release date.

sources.title: Introducing Structured Outputs in the API
sources.evidence: August 6, 2024 announcement names the May 13 snapshot as the previous model and documents GPT-4o function calling. It distinguishes function-based schema constraints from new response-format support exclusive at launch to August GPT-4o and mini; later-default capabilities are not assumed for May.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: Complete Markdown lists gpt-4o-2024-05-13 for October 23, 2026 shutdown in the April 22 notice. The later August/November snapshots instead have a January 14, 2027 retirement notice. This is documentary lifecycle evidence, not a live API request.

sources.title: Introducing gpt-oss
sources.evidence: Full indexed primary article was readable after direct retrieval timed out. Its August 5, 2025 release identifies gpt-oss as the first open-weight language models since GPT-2 and describes GPT-4o as proprietary. Its parameter table belongs to gpt-oss, not GPT-4o.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current API service terms effective January 1, 2026 grant limited service access and reserve OpenAI intellectual property. Supports a descriptive proprietary classification; not a checkpoint license or a claim these exact terms governed the May 2024 release.

sources.title: GPT-4o System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh full August 2024 card fetched October 27 and text-searched for model size, parameters and numeric disclosures. Describes autoregressive multimodal training, but publishes neither nominal total nor active parameters. Its research/ChatGPT audio checkpoints do not supply a count for gpt-4o-2024-05-13.

sources.title: Toward understanding and preventing misalignment generalization
sources.evidence: Fresh full paper fetched October 27 and relevant appendices reread. Appendix G.3 identifies gpt-4o-2024-08-06; Appendix D Table 3 gives 2.1-million SAE latents and 64 nonzero latents per token. These are an auxiliary autoencoder dictionary and sparsity setting, not GPT-4o total or active parameters, and the later snapshot is not substituted for May.

sources.title: GPT-5 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh full card fetched October 27 and GPT-4o comparisons plus parameter/size terms rechecked. Its tables concern capability and safety scores, including the most recent GPT-4o; they provide no total or active count for the exact May snapshot.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 Prompting Guide
sources.evidence: Guide explicitly calls GPT-4o a prior non-reasoning model. This supports a family-level description but does not identify gpt-4o-2024-05-13; the exact dated snapshot assertion is left unresolved under this audit's variant-specific standard.

sources.title: Helpful assistant features suppress emergent misalignment
sources.evidence: December 2025 interpretability research describes GPT-4o base residual-stream activations and the earlier SAE methodology. It supplies no production count or exact May-snapshot architecture; an auxiliary latent count is not a model parameter count.

sources.title: DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence
sources.evidence: Original June 2024 research report reopened October 27. Table 2 defines #TP as total parameters and #AP as active parameters. Tables 3 and 4 explicitly list GPT-4o-0513 with a dash in both columns; no nominal total or active count is provided. These are DeepSeek comparison conventions, not OpenAI size disclosures.

sources.title: HELMET: How to Evaluate Long-Context Language Models Effectively and Thoroughly
sources.evidence: Original proceedings PDF reopened October 27. Appendix C Table 15 (PDF page 43) names gpt-4o-2024-05-13 exactly and marks # Params as unknown. The caption states active/total notation for MoE models, but supplies neither count for this snapshot. A bounded fresh search for exact May-snapshot total/active counts and later 2025-2026 research found no supported nominal specification.

name.note: The catalog date suffix identifies the first dated GPT-4o API snapshot, not the current alias or a later ChatGPT/realtime model.

developer.note: OpenAI publishes and releases this model; Microsoft is a provider, not its developer.

family.note: Use the specifically named GPT-4o family instead of generic GPT.

release_date.note: Dated launch explicitly made text/vision GPT-4o available in the API that day; subsequent official documentation identifies the initial May snapshot separately.

open_weights.note: Released through hosted services; later OpenAI open-weight release history corroborates that this intervening model was not an open checkpoint.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the closed hosted model, not an SPDX license or a claim of downloadable weights.

parameters_b.note: No supported nominal total was found in the refreshed OpenAI disclosures or exact-snapshot original comparison tables. DeepSeek-Coder-V2 lists GPT-4o-0513 total as a dash; HELMET lists gpt-4o-2024-05-13 parameters as unknown. No sibling count, speculative estimate or auxiliary SAE latent count is adopted.

active_parameters_b.note: No supported nominal active count was found independently of total. DeepSeek-Coder-V2 explicitly leaves GPT-4o-0513 #AP blank with a dash, and HELMET provides no count. Neither assumed dense/MoE structure nor SAE sparsity supplies the missing model specification.

architecture.note: The launch topic tag says Transformers, but its text and inspected technical sources do not establish exact May-snapshot structure. Later residual-stream research uses the August snapshot; it is not transferred. No dense/MoE classification is inferred.

context_window.note: The exact-version Microsoft provider row gives 128,000, corroborating the OpenAI family context. The May version has a separate 4,096 output cap; later snapshots have 16,384. No binary 131,072 substitution.

modalities.note: These were the publicly released May API modalities. Native audio/video and image generation demonstrations of the wider GPT-4o project do not establish them for this immutable API identifier.

reasoning.note: General reasoning capability is not a dedicated reasoning mode. Later first-party non-reasoning descriptions name the GPT-4o family without binding this May snapshot; clear the unsupported exact-version false rather than infer it.

tool_call.note: Exact May provider row explicitly supports parallel function calling, corroborated by OpenAI historical GPT-4o function-call availability. This is historical model capability despite endpoint shutdown.

patch.notes: Specifications describe gpt-4o-2024-05-13, the initial text/vision API snapshot, not later GPT-4o, ChatGPT, audio or realtime variants. Its documented context is 128,000 tokens with a separate 4,096-token output limit. OpenAI lists this snapshot as shut down October 23, 2026; no live endpoint call was made. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed; original DeepSeek-Coder-V2 and HELMET comparisons leave the exact May snapshot counts unknown. Exact architecture and dedicated reasoning-mode classification remain unverified; a launch topic tag, later unpinned family descriptions and August-snapshot interpretability research are not substituted for exact May evidence.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter-only re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts after reopening OpenAI launch, API documentation, system cards and interpretability research. DeepSeek-Coder-V2 explicitly leaves both counts blank for GPT-4o-0513; the later HELMET original table also marks the exact snapshot size unknown. No supported nominal count emerged from bounded later research searches. Preserve all other 12 field assessments and prior corrections.
